title: Cheap Drones Remain Wild Card in Iran war

title: Air Canada C.E.O. Draws Scorn for Delivering Condolences Only in English
partialText: The lack of French in Michael Rousseau’s speech about the deadly collision at LaGuardia Airport reignited a debate over linguistic inclusivity in Canada.

title: Supreme Court Sides With Internet Provider in Copyright Fight Over Pirated Music
partialText: Leading music labels sued Cox Communications for failing to terminate accounts of subscribers flagged for distributing copyrighted music.

partialText: Moscow’s forces are intensifying their attacks in southern Ukraine after Kyiv made rare gains along the front.

partialText: F.B.I. agents thought they had weakened an online hate group known as the Base. A string of European terrorism cases indicates it has resurged.

title: A Day in the Life of a New York City Junklugger

partialText: Within the Senate’s housing bill lie the terms of an unusual debate: Who gets to own — and live in — single-family homes?

title: Why This City’s Reckoning With Cesar Chavez Is So Complicated
partialText: San Jose, Calif., is where Mr. Chavez began organizing in the 1950s, and he once lived there. After revelations of sexual abuse by the labor leader, the city and his old neighborhood are confronting his legacy.

title: A Critical Political Season Could Decide if Alaska Is a Failed ‘Petrostate’

title: Some States Already Preparing for Potential Supreme Court Ban on Late Ballots
partialText: The court’s conservatives appear skeptical of laws allowing mail ballots to arrive after Election Day. A decision could come as late as June, potentially scrambling midterm elections.

title: The Brigade System Helps Restaurants Succeed. Does It Also Lead to Abuse?
partialText: Allegations against Noma’s chef have spurred debate over whether a 19th-century model for organizing kitchen staffs breeds physical and psychic violence.

title: It Begins as a Tick Bite and Can Be Devastating. And It’s Spreading.
partialText: The incidence of alpha-gal syndrome appears to be growing significantly. Patients who are bitten can develop a severe allergy to red meat, and a few have died.
